name: Jalupro

lead: Jalupro is a brand of injectable skin boosters that combine an amino acid blend with hyaluronic acid. Clinics offer it to improve skin quality: hydration, firmness, fine lines, glow, and areas like under-eyes, neck and hands, rather than adding volume.

The amino acids named for it (glycine, proline, leucine, lysine) are building blocks of collagen, and the marketed idea is that they support fibroblasts, the cells that make collagen and elastin. Published human trials of the brand itself are not described in the sources found.

paras: A practitioner chooses a product (Classic, HMW, Super Hydro, Young Eye or Glow Peel), numbs the area and gives a series of tiny injections. A course is typically four sessions two to four weeks apart, with maintenance suggested about every four months.

Reported effects are a prickling feeling, temporary redness, mild swelling and pinpoint bruising for hours to a couple of days. People with certain medical conditions, active infections or allergies are advised to consult a practitioner first. Regulatory status varies by country and product.

chain: Amino acids and hyaluronic acid injected into the skin
angle.text: People use Jalupro to improve skin texture and glow without adding volume. The marketed route is hydration from hyaluronic acid plus amino acids that are collagen building blocks.

lead: Jalupro is a range of injectable skin boosters that combine an amino acid complex with hyaluronic acid, described by clinics as a biorevitalisant. The idea is to nourish fibroblasts, the cells that produce collagen and elastin, and to hydrate the skin.[1]

Variants include Classic (amino acids with low molecular weight hyaluronic acid for face and body), Young Eye for under-eye lines and dark circles, Super Hydro for deeper structure, HMW with high molecular weight hyaluronic acid, and Glow Peel for superficial treatment.[1] Clinics also sell an oral amino acid supplement alongside the injections.[1]
In looksmaxxing circles it is grouped with hardmaxx procedures: in-clinic skin quality treatments as opposed to fillers that add volume.[1]

paras: Clinic guides describe Jalupro as an injectable that supports skin quality rather than adding structural volume. Classic is used on face and body areas such as the abdomen, knees, inner thighs, scars and stretch marks; Young Eye on the under-eye; Super Hydro on deeper facial areas; HMW on face, neck, décolletage, hands and lips.[1] The brand's approach is called Amino Acid Replacement Therapy, and sources differ on the manufacturer name, with some crediting Professional Dietetics and others a Swiss company.[1]

A consultation is followed by topical numbing and a series of small injections, with the visit taking about an hour. A course is four treatments spaced two to four weeks apart, with results said to last about six months and maintenance suggested around every four months.[1] Most people feel a light prickling and may have temporary redness, swelling or pinpoint bruising that settles within hours to days.[1]

A 2024 cost-effectiveness analysis in the Journal of Wound Care examined topical hyaluronic acid and amino acids in hard-to-heal wounds, and a 2025 Italian study looked at moisture-associated skin damage in neonates; these concern wound care rather than cosmetic injections.[2][3]
No studies found of Jalupro as a cosmetic injectable. Related studies of hyaluronic acid with amino acids in wound care exist.[2][3]
